classification.difficultyReason: Use the given derivative cue to recognise a logarithmic antiderivative, then evaluate a definite integral.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Differentiate $x^2+1$, and hence find the area under the graph $y=\dfrac{x}{x^2+1}$, between $x=0$ and $x=2$. Give the exact area and an approximation to 3 decimal places.

answer.worked:
$$\frac{d}{dx}(x^2+1)=2x.$$
Since the numerator is half the derivative of the denominator,
$$\int\frac{x}{x^2+1}\,dx=\frac12\ln(x^2+1)+C.$$
The curve is non-negative on $0\le x\le2$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\int_0^2\frac{x}{x^2+1}\,dx\\&=\left[\frac12\ln(x^2+1)\right]_0^2\\&=\frac12\ln5-\frac12\ln1\\&=\frac12\ln5\\&\approx0.805\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Differentiate $x^2+2x+3$, and hence find the area under the graph $y=\dfrac{x+1}{x^2+2x+3}$, between $x=0$ and $x=1$.

answer.worked:
$$\frac{d}{dx}(x^2+2x+3)=2x+2=2(x+1).$$
Since the numerator is half the derivative of the denominator,
$$\int\frac{x+1}{x^2+2x+3}\,dx=\frac12\ln(x^2+2x+3)+C.$$
The curve is positive on $0\le x\le1$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\int_0^1\frac{x+1}{x^2+2x+3}\,dx\\&=\left[\frac12\ln(x^2+2x+3)\right]_0^1\\&=\frac12\ln6-\frac12\ln3\\&=\frac12\ln2\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
